assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed how trade is modelled, measured and taught. It moved the field from representative-firm models to models of within-industry reallocation and gains from trade, and it underpins a large body of empirical work on productivity and trade liberalisation.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the core heterogeneous-firm contribution. Helpman's earlier monopolistic-competition trade theory and later firm-level work are the natural complement. Redding and others have been influential in quantification and extensions, but the core credit is concentrated in two names.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation through firm-level microdata, structural extensions and policy use. The field has had time to test and refine the central predictions, so the case is mature.
uncertainties: The Committee may weigh Helpman's earlier new-trade-theory contributions and the claims of Krugman-era work differently than I do.
Whether Redding should be included, and how credit is divided with the quantitative trade tradition (B037).
Some predictions of the baseline model are rejected in detail, though it has been widely extended.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the evidence on trade shocks reshaped understanding of wage inequality, labour-market polarisation and the distributional costs of globalisation. The work is empirically credible, widely replicated and policy-relevant.
assessment.attribution: Autor (tasks and polarisation, import competition) and Katz (skill-biased change and the race between education and technology) are central. Hanson and Dorn are central to the trade-shock strand. Any three-person limit forces a choice between the technology strand and the trade-shock strand.
assessment.maturity: Roughly two decades for the skill-premium and task literature and over a decade for the China-shock results. These have been extensively tested, and the long-run adjustment findings are still being refined.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 inequality-and-institutions prize and with the recent Nobel emphasis on labour and causal methods.
The persistence and interpretation of the trade-shock effects are still debated.
The three-name limit may leave out Dorn or the earlier task-framework contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Random-coefficients demand estimation with endogenous prices (BLP) and dynamic industry models became the standard toolkit for merger analysis, antitrust and empirical industrial organisation. The methodological and applied impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: The BLP trio has a clear and widely recognised claim for demand estimation. Pakes also made foundational dynamic-oligopoly and estimation contributions. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are plausible additional names, so selecting three is a judgement.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use in academic work and in regulatory and legal practice, with extensive refinements. The case is mature.
uncertainties: The three-name limit versus broader credit to Bresnahan and the dynamic-games strand.
Some committee members may weigh methodology less than a substantive discovery.
Identification of structural models rests on strong functional-form assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work formalised how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. It created much of modern political economics and is empirically as well as theoretically influential.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the closest to a unified research programme (the books on political economics and on constitutions). Besley is central on state capacity and political accountability. Credit is shared and well documented, though others, such as Acemoglu and Robinson, have already been recognised in a nearby area.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of development, strongly confirmed by theory and empirics. Citations and subsequent literatures are extensive.
uncertainties: Disclosed conflict: the profile notes a corruption paper co-authored with Persson and Rothstein, and Persson is a Stockholm colleague in the wider community. This is disclosed, not adjudicated.
Thematic proximity to the 2024 prize on institutions may count for or against.
Empirical identification of constitutional effects is harder than for natural-experiment work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The sufficient-statistics approach, the elasticity of taxable income and tax-responsiveness evidence connected optimal tax theory to empirical estimates. It changed how tax and transfer policy is analysed and evaluated.
assessment.attribution: Saez and Slemrod are central to the ETI and tax-avoidance strands, and Chetty to the sufficient-statistics methodology. Feldstein, who is deceased, and Mirrlees, who is already recognised, are precursors. Attributing a clean three-person credit is difficult.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of evidence and use in policy design, although the largest elasticities are still contested.
uncertainties: Overlap with B039 and B044, which share Saez and Chetty.
Parameter estimates are sensitive to method, which weakens claims of settled empirical conclusions.
Relative weight of the contribution against Mirrlees-style theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measuring misallocation of inputs across firms gave a quantitative account of why countries differ in income and productivity. It bridged micro data and growth accounting and shaped development and growth research.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) are the central pair. Restuccia and Rogerson's framework is a closely related parallel contribution. Credit is reasonably clear but depends on how the Committee treats the shared framework.
assessment.maturity: Seventeen years of extension and application. Measurement-error and interpretation critiques are active, which tempers maturity.
uncertainties: Measured misallocation can partly reflect measurement error or unmodelled frictions.
The Committee may regard the programme as still developing relative to the older candidates above.
Possible additional credit to Rogerson, who is not on the candidate list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Household leverage and mortgage credit were shown, with granular data, to drive credit booms, consumption collapses and unemployment. This changed the understanding of the 2008 crisis and of the role of household balance sheets in the business cycle.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are a well-defined duo with a clear, joint research programme. The inclusion of Campbell on the candidate list is a looser fit to the described discovery.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of work. The core findings have been replicated across countries, but it is more recent than the other mature candidates.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises.
Debate about causality of household debt versus broader financial-sector channels.
It may be early relative to the older programmes on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design generalised mechanism design to the control of information, with applications in regulation, platforms and organisational communication. It is a conceptually clean, high-impact theory.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow (2011) introduced the persuasion framework. Bergemann and Morris developed information design and robust predictions. The three-name limit forces a choice between the two strands.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of theory with growing applications. The empirical confirmation is thinner than for the higher-ranked candidates.
uncertainties: Which strand and which names the Committee would credit.
Applied evidence is still limited.
Relationship to earlier work on information and mechanism design, which has already been recognised by the Prize.
